label: Lipid Breakdown
summary: Break down fats that no other part of the cell can handle, and build bile acids (which make fat absorbable) and DHA (a key brain fat) in the process
description: Peroxisomes break down fats that no other part of the cell can handle, and build bile acids (which make fat absorbable) and DHA (a key brain fat) in the process.

parts.label: Breakdown (beta-oxidation) of Very Long Chain Fatty Acids (VLCFAs)
parts.panelTitle: Breakdown (beta-oxidation) of Very Long Chain Fatty Acids (VLCFAs)
parts.text: Peroxisomes break down VLCFAs (fatty acids that are 22 carbons or longer), which mitochondria cannot process, and hand the shortened products off to mitochondria to finish the job.
left: **[X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** the transporter that feeds VLCFAs into the peroxisome (ABCD1) fails, so VLCFAs build up in blood and tissue, damaging the adrenal glands and the brain's white matter.

**[Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders (PBDs)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** when peroxisomes fail to form, VLCFAs build up throughout the body. An elevated blood level of the 26-carbon fatty acid C26:0 is the standard first screening test for Zellweger Spectrum Disorders.

**[Single-enzyme disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** ACOX1 deficiency and D-bifunctional protein (HSD17B4) deficiency each block one step of the beta-oxidation pathway and cause severe infantile neurological disease that closely resembles Zellweger Spectrum Disorder ([Ferdinandusse 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16385454/)).
furtherReading: [Wanders 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33417207/) (pathway overview)
[Engelen 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22889154/) (X-ALD clinical overview)
[Wanders and Waterham 2006](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.biochem.74.082803.133329) (biochemistry of mammalian peroxisomes)
[Wanders 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biochi.2013.08.022) (metabolic functions of peroxisomes in health and disease)
right: **[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease):** VLCFA oxidation fails in brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)) and in human postmortem cortex the fats peroxisomes normally break down are higher in the most severely affected brains than in mildly affected ones ([Kou 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21594711/)). Blocking peroxisomal beta-oxidation in rats increases VLCFAs and amyloid-beta in the brain ([Shi 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neulet.2012.08.086)).
**[Multiple sclerosis](#/diseases/brain-nerve/multiple-sclerosis-ms):** VLCFA oxidation fails in brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)).
**[Cancer:](#/diseases/cancer)** melanoma cells that survive BRAF/MEK inhibitor treatment depend on ACOX1-driven fatty acid oxidation ([Shen 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108421)).

**[Cancer:](#/diseases/cancer)** acute myeloid leukemia cells raise ABCD1 and depend on peroxisomal breakdown of very long chain fatty acids; blocking the transporter kills them selectively in mice ([Parfenova 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41746867/)).

parts.label: Breakdown (alpha-oxidation) of branched fats such as phytanic acid
parts.panelTitle: Breakdown (alpha-oxidation) of branched fats such as phytanic acid
parts.text: Phytanic acid, a branched fat from dairy, ruminant meat and some fish, carries a side branch that blocks normal breakdown. Peroxisomes clip off one carbon (alpha-oxidation) to make pristanic acid, which is then broken down by peroxisomal beta-oxidation.
left: **[Refsum disease](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** variants in PHYH (the alpha-oxidation enzyme) or PEX7 (the receptor that imports the enzyme) block alpha-oxidation. Phytanic acid builds up and causes retinitis pigmentosa (progressive vision loss), loss of smell, nerve damage and unsteady gait, typically starting in late childhood or adulthood. Restricting dietary phytanic acid is the main treatment ([Wanders 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21683154/)).

**[AMACR deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** AMACR flips pristanic acid and bile acid intermediates into the mirror-image form that beta-oxidation enzymes can use. Its loss causes an adult-onset nerve disorder ([Ferdinandusse 2000](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10655068/)).

**[PBDs and RCDP type 1](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** phytanic acid is increased in both, because the alpha-oxidation enzyme depends on PEX7-mediated import; phytanic acid levels also depend on diet and age, so they are less useful for diagnosis in infants.
furtherReading: [Wanders 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21683154/) (alpha-oxidation and disease)
right: **[Prostate cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** AMACR is elevated distinctively enough in prostate tumors to be used as a routine diagnostic marker in pathology labs ([Luo 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11956072/); [Rubin 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11926890/)), linking this pathway to tumor growth and redox stress ([Kong 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32760737/)).

**[Prostate cancer risk and diet](#/diseases/cancer):** dairy and red meat, the main dietary sources of phytanic acid, have been proposed as a link between diet and prostate cancer risk. Epidemiological evidence is limited and mixed: a small case-control study found higher serum phytanic acid in men with prostate cancer, while two larger prospective studies found no overall association ([Price 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20427733/); [Wright 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25132681/)).

parts.label: Production (beta-oxidation) of bile acids
parts.text: Peroxisomes trim the 27-carbon precursors the liver makes from cholesterol (DHCA and THCA) down to the 24-carbon bile acids (cholic and chenodeoxycholic acid). The gut then uses bile acids to absorb fats and fat-soluble vitamins.
left: **[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** the 27-carbon intermediates accumulate in blood and are thought to contribute to liver disease. Oral cholic acid (Cholbam) was approved by the FDA in 2015 as an add-on treatment for peroxisomal disorders including Zellweger Spectrum Disorder; a clinical study found it lowered the toxic intermediates in some patients but cautioned against use in advanced liver disease ([Berendse 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27469511/)).

**[Single-enzyme disorders:](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27647924/)** AMACR, ACOX2 and D-bifunctional protein deficiencies increase levels of 27-carbon bile acid intermediates, and liver injury can be the presenting sign in ACOX2 deficiency ([Vilarinho 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27647924/)).
furtherReading: [Ferdinandusse 2009](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17034878/) (peroxisomes in bile acid synthesis)
right: **[Liver disease](#/diseases/liver):** no common condition has yet been tied specifically to the peroxisomal steps of bile acid synthesis; these steps are linked to rare inherited disease only. Bile acid signaling is an active drug target in cholestatic and fatty liver disease, so peroxisome-specific bile acid intermediates are a candidate biomarker worth testing.

parts.label: Production (beta-oxidation) of DHA
parts.text: Production of DHA (docosahexaenoic acid), the brain and retina's key omega-3 fat, is finished in the peroxisome: a 24-carbon precursor made in the endoplasmic reticulum is shortened by one round of peroxisomal beta-oxidation to 22-carbon DHA.
left: **[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** DHA is markedly reduced in the brain and retina of patients. A randomized trial of DHA supplementation in Zellweger Spectrum Disorders found no clinical benefit on vision or development ([Paker 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20805528/)).

**[D-bifunctional protein deficiency:](#/diseases/genetic-disorders/single-enzyme-disorders)** patient cells cannot complete this final chain-shortening step, so DHA is low ([Su 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11500517/)).
furtherReading: [Ferdinandusse 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11734571/) (identifies the peroxisomal step in DHA synthesis)
[Salem 2001](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11745-001-0805-6) (how DHA acts in the nervous system)
[Belkouch 2016](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnutbio.2016.03.002) (DHA and the hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease)
[Pan 2015](https://doi.org/10.2174/157488471003150820151532) (DHA and the blood-brain barrier in Alzheimer's disease)
right: **[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease):** DHA-containing plasmalogens are reduced in Alzheimer's brain tissue ([Han 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11359882/)). Whether impaired peroxisomal DHA production contributes to this reduction is not established.

**[Retinal degeneration](#/diseases/brain-nerve/vision-and-hearing-loss):** low DHA in photoreceptor membranes is linked to vision loss in genetic peroxisomal disorders. Mice lacking peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzymes developed photoreceptor and retinal pigment epithelium degeneration ([Swinkels 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10631513/)), but omega-3 supplementation did not slow progression to advanced age-related macular degeneration in the AREDS2 trial, so a contribution to common retinal disease is unproven.

label: Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)
summary: Make a family of membrane fats that no other part of the cell can build
description: Peroxisomes make a family of membrane fats that no other part of the cell can build.

parts.label: Building ether lipids and plasmalogens (a job shared with the endoplasmic reticulum)
parts.panelTitle: Building ether lipids and plasmalogens (a job shared with the endoplasmic reticulum)
parts.text: Peroxisomes provide the first steps of building ether lipids and plasmalogens, with the endoplasmic reticulum finishing the molecule. The finished fats end up unusually concentrated in the insulation around nerve fibers (myelin), heart muscle and sperm.
left: **[Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata (RCDP)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** caused by variants in peroxisomal genes that block plasmalogen synthesis. Children have shortening of the upper arms and thighs (rhizomelia, the feature the disorder is named for), cataracts, skeletal changes and severe developmental delay present from birth ([Braverman 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22627108/)).
**[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** plasmalogens are reduced, and a low red blood cell plasmalogen level is a standard diagnostic test.
furtherReading: [Luoma 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25801291/) (plasmalogens protect nerve insulation from oxidative damage)
[Braverman 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22627108/) (functions of plasmalogens in health and disease)
[Honsho and Fujiki 2017](https://doi.org/10.1002/1873-3468.12743) (how plasmalogen synthesis is regulated)
right: **[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease):** plasmalogen synthesis fails in Alzheimer's brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)), alongside broader loss of nerve-insulating lipids ([Han 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11359882/)).
**[Multiple sclerosis](#/diseases/brain-nerve/multiple-sclerosis-ms):** plasmalogen synthesis also fails in MS brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)).
**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** plasmalogens drop in brain and blood with age, correlating with cognitive decline ([Curran 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022227525001889)).

parts.label: Antioxidant protection
parts.text: The vinyl-ether bond in plasmalogens reacts readily with oxidants, so plasmalogens are thought to absorb oxidative damage that would otherwise affect the rest of the membrane.
left: **[RCDP and Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders)**: cells lacking plasmalogens are more vulnerable to oxidative damage. The clearest evidence comes from ether lipid-deficient cells and mouse models ([Perez 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36178986/)), rather than from patient fibroblasts.
furtherReading: [Zou 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32939090/) (peroxisome-made ether lipids and ferroptosis)
[Dean 2018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28523433/) (ether lipid functions)
right: **[Cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** the peroxisomal enzyme AGPS builds ether lipids that fuel cancer cell migration, invasion and survival signals across multiple tumor types ([Chen 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51489-1)). The same ether lipids can make tumor cells more vulnerable to ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid oxidation ([Zou 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32939090/)).
**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** falling plasmalogen levels influence cell-death sensitivity in aging tissues ([Curran 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022227525001889)).

**[Viral infection](#/diseases/infection):** some enveloped viruses expand peroxisomes and take over ether lipid and plasmalogen production to build their own membranes ([Ferreira 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34696946/)).

**[Parkinson's disease:](#/diseases/brain-nerve)** blood plasmalogens are lower in Parkinson's disease ([Dragonas 2009](https://doi.org/10.1515/cclm.2009.205)), and the lipid composition of frontal cortex membranes is altered ([Fabelo 2011](https://doi.org/10.2119/molmed.2011.00119)). In MPTP mice, plasmalogen augmentation and plasmalogen precursors reduce striatal dopamine loss ([Miville-Godbout 2016](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0151020); [Miville-Godbout 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.brainres.2017.08.020)).

label: Detoxification
summary: Neutralize the damaging by-products of the cell's own chemistry, and clear waste the body cannot leave in circulation
description: Peroxisomes neutralize the damaging by-products of the cell's own chemistry, and clear waste the body cannot leave in circulation.

parts.label: Glyoxylate disposal
parts.text: Glyoxylate is a metabolic by-product that turns into oxalate, which crystallizes into kidney stones if not cleared. The peroxisomal enzyme AGXT converts glyoxylate into the harmless amino acid glycine. Silencing glycolate oxidase, the peroxisomal enzyme that makes glyoxylate, is the basis of an approved drug that switches the enzyme off.
left: **[Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1 (PH1)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** loss of AGXT causes oxalate to accumulate and crystallize, damaging the kidneys and, as kidney function decreases, other organs.
**[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** calcium oxalate kidney stones also occur in some patients ([van Woerden 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16621644/)).
furtherReading: [Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/) (PH1 and peroxisomal enzyme targeting)
[Garrelfs 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33789010/) (phase 3 trial of lumasiran)
right: **[Kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** most kidney stones in the general population are calcium oxalate. Lumasiran (approved by the FDA in 2020 for PH1) silences glycolate oxidase (HAO1) in the liver, making it an approved drug that works by targeting a peroxisomal enzyme ([Garrelfs 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33789010/)).

parts.label: Hydrogen peroxide and reactive oxygen species (ROS)
parts.panelTitle: Hydrogen peroxide and reactive oxygen species (ROS)
parts.text: Peroxisomal fat breakdown generates hydrogen peroxide, which catalase neutralizes inside the same compartment. Controlled leakage of hydrogen peroxide may also act as a signal that reports the cell's metabolic state. Peroxisomes also handle reactive nitrogen species (RNS).
left: **[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** catalase cannot be imported and stays in the cytosol, leaving empty peroxisome membranes ('ghosts'). Catalase location in patient cells is a classic diagnostic readout.

**[Acatalasemia](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** inherited loss of catalase (CAT gene) is usually mild; some individuals develop mouth ulcers, and an increased frequency of diabetes has been reported in catalase-deficient families ([Góth 2000](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11117918/)).
furtherReading: [Lismont 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31357514/) (peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide as a signal)
[Fransen 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbadis.2011.12.001) (peroxisomes in ROS and RNS metabolism)
[He 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcb.2021.02.005) (peroxisomes as adaptors to metabolic and environmental stress)
[Giorgio 2007](https://doi.org/10.1038/nrm2240) (hydrogen peroxide as a signal in ageing)
right: **[Cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** in lymphoma, peroxisomes buffer free radicals generated by cancer drugs, letting tumor cells survive otherwise lethal treatment ([Dahabieh 2017](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5635217/)).

**[Neurodegeneration](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** PEX5 import defects and catalase loss compromise detoxification of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in neurodegenerative disease ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Diabetic kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** kidneys develop structurally intact but functionally 'empty' peroxisomes; loss of the DsbA-L/catalase complex disables local antioxidant defense and accelerates damage ([Liu 2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213231723002562)).

**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** in fat tissue, peroxisome-derived ROS stabilize PEX2, which degrades the fat-releasing enzyme ATGL and suppresses fat breakdown ([Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/)).

**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** catalase is mislocalized to the cytosol in aged and replicatively senescent cells, reducing peroxisomal antioxidant capacity ([Kim 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39398621/)).

parts.label: D-amino acid handling
parts.text: The peroxisomal enzyme D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO) breaks down D-serine, a mirror-image amino acid that the brain uses to boost signaling through NMDA receptors, which are central to learning and memory. DAAO activity helps set how much D-serine is available.
left: To our knowledge, no human disorder caused by DAAO deficiency has been described.
furtherReading: [Terry-Lorenzo 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39756412/) (D-amino acid oxidase inhibitors in human clinical trials)
[Paul and De Belleroche 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00726-012-1385-9) (D-amino acids in ALS)
right: **Schizophrenia:** reduced NMDA receptor signaling is a leading hypothesis, and DAAO inhibitors have been tested in clinical trials to raise D-serine ([Terry-Lorenzo 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39756412/)).
**ALS:** a DAAO variant (R199W) was identified in a family with inherited ALS ([Mitchell 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20368421/)).

label: Organelle Crosstalk
summary: Physically make contact with other compartments and hand material back and forth
description: Peroxisomes physically make contact with other compartments and hand material back and forth.

parts.label: Mitochondria
parts.text: Peroxisomes pass partially broken-down fats to mitochondria to finish beta-oxidation, and mitochondria in some peroxisome-deficient cells are visibly abnormal.
left: **[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** some of the cellular damage in peroxisomal disease is inflicted second-hand, through structurally and functionally abnormal mitochondria in peroxisome-deficient cells ([Baumgart 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11583975/)).

**[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** when peroxisome biogenesis fails, orphaned peroxisomal membrane proteins are rerouted to mitochondria and tagged for disposal by MUL1 and MARCH5, a backup quality-control system that clears them before they accumulate ([Segev-Nakar 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42270660/)).
furtherReading: [Schrader 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25687155/) (peroxisome-mitochondria interplay in disease)
[Schrader 2020](https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12083) (organelle interplay: peroxisome interactions in health and disease)
[Ravi 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.devcel.2021.04.019) (PI5P4Ks and peroxisome-mitochondria interplay)
[Tanaka 2019](https://doi.org/10.1242/jcs.224766) (peroxisomes control mitochondrial dynamics and apoptosis)
right: **[Viral infection](#/diseases/infection):** peroxisome positioning and contact patterns are remodeled over the course of infection, suggesting viruses may rewire peroxisome-mitochondria crosstalk to favor replication or immune evasion ([Cook 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32488-6)).

**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** aging weakens peroxisome-mitochondria contacts, disrupting lipid transfer and accelerating mitochondrial breakdown and muscle aging ([Scalabrin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64833-w)).

**[Diabetic kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** peroxisomal fat breakdown produces succinate, which disrupts mitochondrial energy production and generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) ([Wang 2022](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8881667/)).

parts.label: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)
parts.text: Peroxisomes draw raw material from the ER, the cell's membrane-building factory. Tether proteins (such as ACBD5) on the peroxisome and VAPB on the ER hold the two together so lipids can move between them.
left: **[ACBD5 deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** loss of the peroxisome-ER tether causes retinal degeneration and white matter disease with raised VLCFAs ([Ferdinandusse 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27799409/)).

**[PBDs caused by PEX3, PEX16 or PEX19](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** these genes build the peroxisome membrane itself. Patient cells in these groups lack even the empty membrane 'ghosts' found in most other Zellweger groups ([Honsho 1998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9837814/)), and the presentation is usually at the severe end, though milder PEX16 cases have been reported ([Kumar 2018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30094183/)).
furtherReading: [Costello 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28108524/) (ACBD5-VAPB peroxisome-ER tether)
[Castro 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibs.2018.01.001) (peroxisome contact sites in disease)
right: **[Neurodegeneration](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** peroxisome contacts with mitochondria and the ER help shape the lipid composition of synaptic membranes ([Carmichael 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40621503/)).
**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** aging weakens peroxisome contacts with the ER and mitochondria, disrupting lipid transfer ([Scalabrin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64833-w)).

parts.label: Lipid droplets
parts.text: Peroxisomes tap directly into stored fat droplets for fuel. During fasting, peroxisomes move to lipid droplets and help switch on fat release.
left: No genetic peroxisomal disorder has been defined by a lipid droplet contact defect. The one disorder defined by a contact site defect, ACBD5 deficiency, involves peroxisome-ER contacts.
furtherReading: [Kong 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31996685/) (PEX5 brings ATGL to peroxisome-lipid droplet contacts)
[Han 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515256420960303) (PEX5 escorts the lipase ATGL to peroxisome-lipid droplet contacts during fasting)
[Lodhi and Semenkovich 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2014.01.002) (peroxisomes as a hub for lipid metabolism and signaling)
right: **[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** during fasting, PEX5 escorts the fat-releasing enzyme ATGL to peroxisome-lipid droplet contact sites, making these contacts important for stimulated fat breakdown ([Han 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515256420960303)).

**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** peroxisome-derived ROS stabilize PEX2, which degrades ATGL and suppresses fat breakdown, so peroxisomes act as fatty-acid sensors that tune storage versus release ([Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/)).

label: Immune & Inflammatory Signaling
summary: Raise the alarm when a virus gets in, and shape how immune cells behave in response
description: Peroxisomes raise the alarm when a virus gets in, and shape how immune cells behave in response.

parts.label: Immune cell behavior and inflammation
parts.text: Immune cells depend heavily on lipid handling to decide what to do, and the brain's resident immune cells (microglia) are particularly sensitive to peroxisomal failure.
left: **[Cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy (childhood cerebral ALD)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** microglial damage appears before major loss of nerve insulation, not after it, meaning inflammation is part of the disease mechanism rather than a downstream reaction ([Bergner 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30980503/)). This is why the disease is treated by replacing the patient's blood-forming stem cells, through transplant or the approved gene therapy (elivaldogene autotemcel).
furtherReading: [Ferreira 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31382586/) (review of peroxisomes in innate immunity)
[Di Cara 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28723556/) (peroxisomes required for macrophage immune function)
[Di Cara 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms20163877) (peroxisomes in immune response and inflammation)
right: **[Brain and nerve disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** the microglial sensitivity to peroxisomal dysfunction seen in ALD now has direct support in Alzheimer's disease: the peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzyme MFE-2 is reduced in microglia from patients and from model mice, and removing it from microglia drives inflammation and amyloid deposition ([Gao 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41162676/)). For Parkinson's disease and MS this remains a hypothesis.

**[Infection (COVID-19)](#/diseases/infection):** mice whose macrophages lack Pex5 had worse outcomes and longer-lasting lung damage, placing peroxisomes in how macrophages resolve inflammation rather than prolong it ([Wei 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40048515/)).

parts.label: Antiviral alarm system
parts.text: An adaptor protein called MAVS, which relays signals from virus-sensing proteins, sits on both peroxisomes and mitochondria. The peroxisomal pool raises the first, fast alarm, and the mitochondrial pool drives the slower, broader response that follows.
left: Whether patients with PBDs are more susceptible to viral infection has not been systematically studied; the human literature is limited to isolated case reports, and those describe bacterial or opportunistic infection. Experiments that placed MAVS only on peroxisomes showed that peroxisomal MAVS alone can launch this fast response ([Dixit 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20451243/)).
furtherReading: [Dixit 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20451243/) (discovery of peroxisomal MAVS signaling)
[Odendall 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24952503/) (peroxisomal MAVS drives type III interferon)
[Ferreira 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34696946/) (review of how viruses exploit peroxisomes)
right: **[Viral infection:](#/diseases/infection)** peroxisomes act as an early antiviral alarm, switching on defense genes that slow infection before the full immune response arrives ([Dixit 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20451243/)) and many viruses reduce peroxisome numbers to silence this early warning system.

label: Metabolic Signaling
summary: Sense fats and help set how much of them the body burns versus stores
description: Peroxisomes sense fats and help set how much of them the body burns versus stores.

parts.label: Peroxisomes supply the fats that switch PPARs on
parts.panelTitle: Peroxisomes supply the fats that switch PPARs on
parts.text: PPARs are nuclear receptors switched on by fatty acids, and peroxisomes make and break down a number of those fatty acids; the peroxisome therefore helps set how much signal the receptors receive.
left: **[ACOX1 deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders/single-enzyme-disorders):** ACOX1 carries out the first step of peroxisomal fat breakdown, and its substrates are themselves PPARα ligands. In mice lacking ACOX1 those substrates are not degraded and PPARα is persistently switched on, followed by liver inflammation and tumors ([Huang 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21801867/)), providing clear genetic evidence that a peroxisomal enzyme sets PPAR signaling rather than only responding to it.

**[Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** when peroxisomes fail to form, the fats that activate PPARs are not processed normally, so the signal supply is disrupted as a downstream consequence rather than a primary cause.
furtherReading: [Kleiboeker and Lodhi 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35988716/) (review of how peroxisomal metabolism regulates whole-body energy balance)
right: **[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes)**: fat cells silenced for the peroxisome factor PEX16 failed to mature, and adding peroxisome-derived lipids together with a PPARgamma agonist restored maturation, so the lipids peroxisomes make feed the receptor that drives fat cell development ([Hofer 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28017862/)).

**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes)**: peroxisomal lipid synthesis in fat tissue generates lipids that activate a nuclear receptor and drive fat storage, reported for LXR rather than PPAR, so the receptor differs but the principle that peroxisomes supply the signal is the same ([Kleiboeker 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38458567/)).

parts.label: PPARs switch on peroxisomal fat-burning genes
parts.panelTitle: PPARs switch on peroxisomal fat-burning genes
parts.text: Once activated, PPARs induce the peroxisomal fat-burning enzymes and transporters, so part of what the receptor does is build more peroxisomal capacity (the name "peroxisome proliferator" comes from this effect, though the effect may be mostly rodent-specific).
left: **[Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** the enzymes PPARα induces aren’t delivered effectively into dysfunctional peroxisomes, so the response is blunted downstream of the receptor.
**[X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** leriglitazone, a brain-penetrant PPARγ agonist, has been studied in clinical trials in adults with X-ALD.
furtherReading: [Tahri-Joutey 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34445672/) (review of how PPARα regulates peroxisomal fatty acid beta-oxidation)
[Gonzalez 2008](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18006136/) (review how the peroxisome proliferation that gave PPARs their name appears to be mostly rodent-specific)
right: **[Cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** AMACR and other PPAR-regulated genes link peroxisomal lipid metabolism to tumor growth; anti-cancer PPAR antagonists may expose peroxisomal vulnerabilities ([Kong 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32760737/)).
**[Diabetes](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** genetic variants that activate PPARγ affect insulin sensitivity and diabetes risk ([Vales-Villamarin 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34887761/)).

**[Liver disease](#/diseases/liver):** lanifibranor has been studied in clinical trials for MASH (fatty liver disease with inflammation), and two PPAR-targeting drugs, elafibranor and seladelpar, received accelerated FDA approval in 2024 for primary biliary cholangitis. The share of their benefit that runs through peroxisomes is not known.

**[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** PPARγ agonists rescue cognition in animal models, but a peroxisome-driven mechanism is unproven ([Steinke 2023](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/12/8/1116)).

label: Peroxisome Biogenesis & Recycling
summary: Build new peroxisomes, stock them with enzymes, and recycle the worn-out ones
description: Peroxisomes build new peroxisomes, stock them with enzymes, and recycle the worn-out ones.

parts.label: Import (address-tag delivery)
parts.text: Every enzyme inside a peroxisome is made in the cytosol and carried in through the membrane. Each carries a short address tag (PTS1 or PTS2) that a shuttle receptor reads: PEX5 for PTS1, and PEX7 together with PEX5 for PTS2.
left: **[Zellweger Spectrum Disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** variants in PEX genes disrupt the peroxisome’s import and assembly system, impacting broad peroxisomal function.
**[RCDP type 1](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** loss of PEX7 blocks only PTS2 cargo, which explains why plasmalogen synthesis and alpha-oxidation fail while most other functions are spared.
furtherReading: [Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/) (PH1 enzyme mistargeting)
[Waterham 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26611709/) (overview of peroxisomal disorders)
[Feng 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35768507/) (structure of the PEX2/PEX10/PEX12 channel that recycles PEX5)
[Fujiki 2020](https://doi.org/10.1242/jcs.236943) (recent insights into peroxisome biogenesis and associated diseases)
[Honsho 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-60204-8_4) (peroxisome biogenesis disorders)
right: **[Kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** primary hyperoxaluria type 1 can be a subtler failure of this system: in some patients, a single variant changes the address tag so a working AGXT enzyme is sent to mitochondria instead of peroxisomes ([Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/)).

**[Multiple sclerosis](#/diseases/brain-nerve/multiple-sclerosis-ms):** neuronal peroxisomes are reduced in the grey matter of people with multiple sclerosis ([Gray 2014](https://doi.org/10.1177/1352458513505691)).

**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** peroxisomal import declines with age in model systems, and experimentally blocking import activates the integrated stress response and shuts down ribosome biogenesis ([Kim 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39398621/)).
**[Neurodegeneration](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** PEX5 import defects compromise ROS detoxification ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Diabetes](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** functional peroxisomes are required for insulin-producing beta-cell integrity; when import fails, beta-cells die even without obvious oxidative stress ([Baboota 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30795913/)).

**[Brain (Sleep)](#/diseases/brain-nerve)**: in the fly brain, peroxisomal import in neuronal glia rises and falls on a daily cycle that peaks in the early morning and depends on the circadian clock and PEX5; reducing PEX5 in those glia caused hyperactivity and less total sleep, and shifted brain lipid composition ([Das 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42455861/))

parts.label: Division
parts.text: Peroxisomes divide to multiply, expanding their numbers as the cell's needs change. PEX11B elongates the membrane and helps assemble the fission proteins, which are shared with mitochondria (DRP1, MFF, FIS1) and pinch the membrane in two. Super-resolution imaging in neurons suggests peroxisomes can also form anew from vesicles budding off mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum, rather than only by division.
left: **[PEX11B deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** a milder PBD with cataracts, hearing loss and short stature, often with normal standard blood tests ([Ebberink 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22581968/)).

**[PEX11B deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** knocking out PEX11B in human iPSC-derived brain cells impaired peroxisome division and shifted lipid composition, altering neural progenitor fate and how the developing tissue organized itself, with mitochondria unaffected ([Bodnya 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42753733/)).

**[DRP1 (DNM1L) and MFF deficiencies](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** these break both peroxisome and mitochondrial division, producing elongated organelles and severe neurological disease ([Waterham 2007](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17460227/)).
furtherReading: [Schrader 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26409486/) (peroxisome division in health and disease)
[Coceano 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41507166/) (mitochondria-derived vesicles contribute to new peroxisome formation in neurons)
[Bodnya 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42753733/) (PEX11B loss in human iPSC brain cells alters neural progenitor fate, with mitochondria unaffected)
right: **[Diabetic neuropathy](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** excess fat chemically modifies PEX11B so peroxisomes cannot elongate and divide, leaving fewer of them in the Schwann cells that insulate peripheral nerves, and driving nerve damage ([Yang 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39934809/)).
**[Viral infection](#/diseases/infection):** infection reshapes peroxisome size, number and positioning over time ([Knoblach 2021](https://www.molbiolcell.org/doi/10.1091/mbc.E21-02-0074)).
**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** as fat cells mature, peroxisome number and function increase ([Hofer 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28017862/)).

parts.label: Recycling (pexophagy)
parts.text: Worn-out or excess peroxisomes are tagged with ubiquitin, engulfed by autophagy and digested so their components can be reused.
left: **[Zellweger Spectrum Disorder](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** in cells with impaired PEX1, ubiquitin-tagged PEX5 builds up on the peroxisome and marks it for destruction, so excess pexophagy contributes to peroxisome loss; blocking pexophagy restored peroxisome function in patient cells ([Law 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28521612/)), pointing to a possible therapeutic route.

**[Zellweger Spectrum Disorder](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** inhibiting USP2, which stabilizes the pexophagy regulator STUB1, reduced runaway pexophagy in PEX1-mutant patient cells, restored peroxisome numbers, eased VLCFA abnormalities and improved movement in PEX1-knockdown flies ([Kim 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42778528/)).
furtherReading: [Zhang 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26344566/) (oxidative stress triggers pexophagy through ATM and PEX5)
[Li 2021](https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2021.814047) (the peroxisome-autophagy redox connection)
right: **[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** quality-control systems clear damaged peroxisomes, preventing them from becoming sources of oxidative damage; these pathways decline with age ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** the peroxisomal E3 ligase PEX2, which marks proteins for destruction, is stabilized by peroxisome-derived ROS in fat tissue ([Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/)).
